headline: Bacterial pathogen diversity shaped by selection, host ancestry, and long-term evolution
label: Bacterial Pathogen Evolution And Genetics
summary: Recent papers link selection on bacterial strain structure, thirty-year lineage evolution, and host ancestry to pathogen genetic diversity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how selection and host-pathogen interaction shape genetic diversity within bacterial populations. A preprint tracking Achromobacter ruhlandii over thirty years examines evolutionary pathways to epidemic lineages. A PLOS Computational Biology study models negative frequency-dependent selection and shows it can generate frequency-dependent epistasis that reinforces or weakens linkage disequilibrium, linking this mechanism to bacterial strain structure. An eLife study in Dar es Salaam relates human genetic ancestry and Mycobacterium tuberculosis diversity to tuberculosis disease severity. Taken together, the work treats pathogen genomic variation as shaped by selection and as bearing on epidemic and clinical outcomes. The thread is dominant rather than uniform, since the tuberculosis study centers on host genetics and disease severity.
